recap.text: Carl goes to his father's master bedroom for the last five minutes of the recording and takes three packs of Marlboro Reds, court documents, a 9mm Glock with two boxes of ammo, and the keys to the motorcycle and Ford truck. Waiting for the fight, he turns the Glock over and admits its overpowered rounds would likely make it explode. Donut asks for a pink holster.

Carl opens his first gold box, a fan box, and finds about 2,000 rounds of ammunition in several boxes, plus an unenchanted black leather shoulder holster of the kind detectives wear on television, with Carl pressed into the leather in English. The holster holds no gun, and Carl knows what the fans want. Donut says they do not know him very well: his father's Glock stays in his inventory, and he has no intention of wearing or using it.

beats.headline: The only gun he had
beats.text: With five minutes left in the recording, Carl goes to the master bedroom so he does not have to listen, and takes everything he can. Three packs of Marlboro Reds from the bottom drawer of the old dresser. A folder of court documents. A 9mm Glock, with two boxes of ammo. The keys to the motorcycle and the Ford truck. Then the dresser itself, the bed and the clothes. His father had only the single gun. A Centipede cabinet stands in the too-small room, and Carl takes that too: his gun, his motorcycle, his arcade cabinet.
beats.gist: Carl takes his father's only gun, a 9mm Glock, and his motorcycle keys.

beats.headline: You're not a gun guy
beats.text: Waiting for the fight, Carl turns his dad's Glock over in his hands. It has been well looked after; his dad always had guns and never let him touch them. Donut sniffs at it: he is not a gun guy. He had training in boot, Carl says, in the Coast Guard. But it came from outside the dungeon. Fired, it would probably explode, because the rounds are overpowered once he handles them, and he would have to adjust each round's yield in his bomber's studio. Donut wants a pink holster for it and suggests Florin. Carl puts the gun away.
beats.gist: Carl turns over his dad's Glock, which Donut sniffs at, and puts it away unfired.

beats.headline: A holster from the fans
beats.text: The first gold box Carl opens is a fan box: several boxes of ammunition, about 2,000 rounds, and an unenchanted black leather shoulder holster of the kind detectives wear on television, with Carl pressed into the leather in English. They do not know you very well, Donut says. The holster holds no gun, but Carl knows what they want him to do. He still has his father's Glock in his inventory, and he has no intention of ever wearing it outside his inventory, or of ever using it.
beats.gist: Carl's first gold box holds a fan holster and ammunition, but he will never wear his father's Glock.
